claims.text: The general distance formula between two points A(x1;y1) and B(x2;y2) is derived by using the theorem of Pythagoras.
claims.quote: To derive a general formula for the distance between two points $A\left({x}_{1};{y}_{1}\right)$ and $B\left({x}_{2};{y}_{2}\right)$ we use the theorem of Pythagoras.

claims.text: By the theorem of Pythagoras applied to the right triangle formed by A, B and C, AB² = AC² + BC², so AB = √(AC²+BC²).
In this right triangle, the horizontal side AC = x2-x1 and the vertical side BC = y2-y1.
Substituting these side lengths gives AB = √(AC²+BC²) = √((x2-x1)²+(y2-y1)²).
The distance d between two points (x1;y1) and (x2;y2) is given by d = √((x1-x2)²+(y1-y2)²).
(x1-x2)² is equal to (x2-x1)², so the order of subtraction in each squared term of the distance formula does not affect the result.
